judgments.reasoning_cat1: An election with a stated default on failure to elect in writing. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Feeds 4(b) and 4(c) coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four numbered consequences, each specific with a bracketed qualification. Nothing vague named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies aggregate margining under Paragraph 4 and the single-agreement effect of Paragraph 12 for separate Principals, which those provisions accommodate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear aggregate-treatment consequences, subject to "any greater requirement imposed by applicable law". Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mirror of 4(b); consistent with Paragraphs 4 and 12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mandatory carve-out for ERISA plan transactions, precisely cross-referenced. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with Paragraph 18 and overrides 4(a)/(c) elections expressly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A deeming and construction rule; long, but each direction is explicit. No named ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It rewrites references to "party" throughout the Agreement, which interacts with Paragraph 11's Event of Default definitions and Paragraph 10's principal representation, but the paragraph states the intended result.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Forward Exposure" is defined as the loss on cancelling and replacing, "determined in accordance with market practice or as otherwise agreed" — a self-consciously indeterminate measure. That is a nameable vagueness at the heart of the annex.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It builds on Market Value and Purchase Date as defined in Paragraph 2 without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonably acceptable to the In-the-Money Party" and the sufficiency test depend on the soft Forward Exposure and Market Value concepts. The mechanics are otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says these rights are in addition to Paragraph 4(a)-(b), so overlap with the ordinary margin regime is expressly handled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive threshold provision requiring prior agreement on the amount. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Paragraph 4(e); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive transaction-by-transaction election, clearly stated. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Paragraph 4(f); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause repeatedly leaves the operative figure as "a specified dollar amount or other specified threshold" to be agreed, so it is inert unless supplemented. That is an open term rather than an ambiguous one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the Margin Notice Deadline definition and 2(e); no conflict located.
judgments.clause_name: Annex V - 2(d) Initial and minimum transfers

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-branch timing rule mirroring Paragraph 4(c); "close of business in the relevant market" is the only elastic phrase. Largely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 2(i) and Paragraph 4(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear return obligation with a proviso preventing a new exposure. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with 2(a) and the Net Unsecured Forward Exposure definition.
judgments.clause_name: Annex V - 2(f) Return on Purchase Date

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Substitution on the Pledgee's acceptance, with "reasonably acceptable" the only soft term. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to Paragraph 9(a); consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Annex V - 2(g) Substitution of Forward Collateral

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad grant covering "any other cash, Securities or property" transferred or due, which is sweeping but expressed as a deliberate catch-all. Little genuine ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is additive to Paragraph 6, though Paragraph 6's premise is that transfers are sales, so the pledge structure here must be read alongside that characterisation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed rehypothecation right with an express proviso preserving return obligations. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Paragraph 8's rehypothecation language and preserves Paragraph 11 duties; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Any covenant or obligation ... under Paragraph 2 or any other provision of this Annex" is broad but the trigger is precise. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly additional to Paragraph 11; consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Annex V - 4(a) Additional Event of Default

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It repeats the "recognized market", "commercially reasonable manner", "reasonably deem satisfactory" and "generally recognized source" formulas, plus a deeming that all Forward Collateral trades in a recognized market — the same open standards that generate liquidation disputes. The named terms are genuinely contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors Paragraph 11(d) and depends on the same Market Value definition, so it carries that provision's tension without adding a distinct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-waiver statement with a specific cross-reference. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly built on Paragraph 17; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A scope and incorporation recital with blanks for the date line filled by hand. Nothing ambiguous in substance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its incorporation is consistent with Annex I paragraph 1, though the precedence claim in the next paragraph competes with Annex I paragraph 2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short precedence rule; the words "any other term of the Agreement" are plain, if very broad. Little internal ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It claims priority over the whole Agreement while Annex I paragraph 2 says Annex I governs and Annex VII claims the same primacy, so the three precedence clauses cannot all be given full effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mandatory identification requirement with two named categories; clear. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with Paragraph 3(b) Confirmation contents and Annex VI paragraph 3; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permits one or two Confirmations; plainly drafted. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 3(b) and Annex VI paragraph 5's recording requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise accrual definition with inclusive/exclusive dates spelled out twice. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It builds on the Paragraph 2(f) Income definition and is used in Annex VI paragraph 7; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An arithmetic definition parallel to Price Differential, with a stated day-count default. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 2(k) and Annex VI paragraph 4(c).
judgments.clause_name: Annex VI - 4(b) Definition of "Sell Back Differential"

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describing "(P + D) - (IR + C)" as "the product of the formula" is a loose use of "product" for a difference, a wording slip in a payment formula. The components are otherwise defined precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex VI paragraph 7 replaces the formula in the market-practice case and paragraphs 10-11 fold Sell Back Price into Repurchase Price references; these overlays require careful reading but are express.
judgments.clause_name: Annex VI - 4(c) Definition of "Sell Back Price"

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two obligations, to agree and to record, each specific; nothing vague. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 3(b) and Annex VI paragraph 4(c)(i).
judgments.clause_name: Annex VI - 5. Agreement on Sell Back Price and Pricing Rate

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A branch-structured termination mechanic with clean cross-references. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with Paragraph 3(c) and Annex VI paragraph 4(c); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The "except to the extent contrary to market practice" carve-out triggers a wholly different formula, so which regime applies depends on an unstated market convention. That is a named soft trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly substitutes for the paragraph 4(c)(ii) formula in that case, so the internal relationship is stated rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It presupposes a repricing occasion without defining when repricing occurs, leaving "at the time of repricing" hanging. A modest gap rather than an ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to an agreement "in Annex I" about non-repricing, but Annex I as executed says nothing on the point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat disapplication of Paragraph 5 plus a specific reverse Income obligation; wording is clear. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts Annex I paragraph 3, which requires Buyer to pass Income to Seller "pursuant to Paragraph 5(i)", and each annex asserts precedence over the other, so the Income allocation for a Buy/Sell Back Transaction is genuinely unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A global construction directive using "as the case may be", which leaves the reader to work out which price applies where. That deferral is a modest source of uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It rewrites Paragraph 2(r) and every Repurchase Price reference, including in Paragraph 11(f)'s cap, so its reach across the instrument requires reconciliation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "In 11 of the Agreement" omits the word "Paragraph", a small mechanical slip, and the directive duplicates paragraph 10's broader rule. The intent is nonetheless recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Annex VI paragraph 10's general construction rule, creating redundancy that could be argued to narrow or widen the earlier direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of "Fund" turns on entities "identified on Schedule VII.A", and the scope clause is otherwise clear. No ambiguous term of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Schedule VII.A is blank and neither named party is an investment company, yet Annex I paragraph 1 makes this Annex applicable and it claims to prevail over any other term, colliding with Annex I paragraph 2 and Annex VI paragraph 1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The per-Fund deeming rules are set out in three lettered specifics after a general statement; the general statement is expressly not limited by them. Reasonably definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies the aggregate margining of Paragraph 4 and the single-agreement and setoff rights of Paragraph 12, an express override that nonetheless has no addressee because Schedule VII.A lists no Fund.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The operative figure is left as a blank "_%", so the primary requirement is unstated and only the 100% floor survives. That is an on-the-face incompleteness in a numeric term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides Paragraph 2(d)'s default Buyer's Margin Percentage, but the second sentence assigns Buyer's Margin Percentage where the Fund is Seller, which reads oddly against Paragraph 2(t)'s Seller's Margin Percentage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two promptness obligations, plainly worded. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Paragraph 3(b) and Paragraph 9; only the empty Schedule VII.A leaves it without application.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but specific, keyed to identified SEC and Investment Company Act rules; "fairly reflect" is the only evaluative phrase. Largely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Paragraph 18(b)'s financial-statement condition without contradicting it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear delivery-to-Custodian mechanic with a special rule where the transferor is the Custodian. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to a Custodian "designated ... in Schedule VII.A", which is blank, and interacts with Paragraph 7 and Paragraph 8 segregation, though without direct contradiction.
judgments.clause_name: Annex VII - 5. Segregation of Purchased Securities

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is an unfilled table heading — no Fund or Custodian is named — so it states an operative premise the document does not supply. That incompleteness is visible on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Annex VII paragraphs 1, 2 and 5 all depend on identifications in this Schedule, and Annex I paragraph 1 declares the Schedule applicable, so the annex framework is left hanging.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause consists of a bracketed instruction, "[insert appropriate language limiting liability of trustees, officers and others]", with the substantive terms never inserted. There is nothing to give effect to.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is made part of the Agreement by Annex I paragraph 1 yet supplies no limitation, leaving Annex VII's Fund framework incomplete rather than contradicted.
